we have shown that the photometric classification server (PCS) is able to produce classifications for stars, galaxies, and quasars with a precision of a few percent, and photometric redshits for galaxies and quasars.

we have developed a system for the classification of objects based on their photometric properties, using the photometry of Pan-STARRs1 and other photometric data, which is able to produce reliable classifications and photometric-redshifts.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the Pan-STARS1 photometry is of sufficient quality to allow the automatic classification and redshift determination of objects at the SDSS spectroscopy limits and fainter, with a precision and accuracy that are similar to the SDSS photometry.

the Pan-STarrs1 photometry is good enough to allow the classification of objects into stars, galaxies and quasars and to estimate photometric redshift for galaxies and quasors with a reasonable precision.

Pan-STARRS-1 will be able to deliver photometric redshift estimates and stellar classifications with the precision of SDSS, and QSO classifications with the same precision as SDSS, but for fainter sources.
